location.selector: window.PEP_PAGE.acts[2].checks[2] (J.limit('a changed loop header. ...') when the first 15 body tokens from for are not exactly 'for ( int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i ++ ) {')

findings.claim: The loop-shape limit misdescribes an unchanged loop. Repro (run on the page headless): the starter's header kept exactly, for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++), with a single unbraced body statement sb.append(i).append(","); gives 'Not supported, line 4: not supported in this practice editor: a changed loop header. Keep the loop exactly as it was: for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) with its body in braces.' The header is not changed; only the braces are absent, and a single-statement body is legal Java by the basic for grammar. The attempt is not counted and nothing is credited, so only the wording is wrong, hence low.

evidence.section: JLS SE 25 14.14.1 The basic for Statement

findings.recommendation: Report the two cases separately: when the header tokens match but the next token is not '{', say 'not supported in this practice editor: a loop body without braces. Put the body in { } as in the starter.'; keep 'a changed loop header' only when the header tokens differ.
